SELECT 
  fish_date_doy,
  COUNT(*) as trips,
  SUM(yt) as total_yt,
  SUM(anglers) as total_anglers,
  ROUND(SUM(yt) / NULLIF(SUM(anglers), 0), 2) as yt_per_angler
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_doy >= 287 AND fish_date_doy <= 301
GROUP BY fish_date_doy
ORDER BY fish_date_doy

# Check the days of week for the key October dates
# We need to see the schedule to infer weekdays
schedule = tables['schedule']
trips = tables['trips']

# Filter October range to see what's scheduled
october_schedule = schedule[
  (schedule['fish_date_doy'] >= 287) & (schedule['fish_date_doy'] <= 301)
]

# Group by fish_date to see patterns (count trips per day tells us which days have boats)
days_with_trips = trips[
  (trips['fish_date_doy'] >= 287) & (trips['fish_date_doy'] <= 301)
].groupby('fish_date_doy').size().sort_index()

print("Days with trips in Oct window (doy 287-301):")
print(days_with_trips)
print("\nTrips data shows consistent activity on these days")

# My committed PTO: d290, d291, d297, d298, d304, d305
